ordered_diagnoses: colorectal liver metastasis with portal vein tumor thrombus

s1.syndrome_frame: liver mass with portal vein tumor thrombus in a patient with history of colon cancer
salient_findings: 25 mm lesion in segment 8 of the liver
liver tumor with solid and cystic components
absence of the right portal vein and perfusion defect throughout the right lobe
key_facts: 55-year-old man
history of moderately differentiated adenocarcinoma of the ascending colon
staged as IIIB (T4N1M0)
no thrombophilic disorders
normal preoperative CEA and CA19-9 levels
completed six months of adjuvant chemotherapy
13 months after surgery, follow-up CT revealed a liver lesion
hepatitis B and C serologies were negative
tumor markers including CEA, CA19-9, α-fetoprotein, and PIVKA-II were all within normal limits
liver tumor with two components: solid and cystic
CTAP showed absence of the right portal vein and a perfusion defect throughout the right lobe

shortlist: colorectal liver metastasis with portal vein tumor thrombus

shortlist.label: liver metastasis from colon cancer
shortlist.why_kept: history of colon cancer and presence of liver lesion with portal vein tumor thrombus

shortlist.label: hepatocellular carcinoma
shortlist.why_kept: liver tumor with solid and cystic components, but less likely given normal tumor markers

shortlist.label: colorectal liver metastasis with portal vein tumor thrombus
shortlist.why_kept: consistent with patient's history and imaging findings

shortlist.label: cystadenocarcinoma
shortlist.why_kept: presence of cystic component in liver tumor, but less common than metastasis

shortlist.label: intrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma
shortlist.why_kept: liver tumor with solid and cystic components, but less likely given absence of biliary communication

raw.rationale: The patient has a history of moderately differentiated adenocarcinoma of the ascending colon and the liver lesion was found 13 months after surgery, which is a common timeframe for metastasis to occur. The presence of a solid and cystic component in the liver tumor and the absence of the right portal vein with a perfusion defect are also consistent with metastasis.

rejected.label: hepatocellular carcinoma
rejected.why: normal tumor markers including α-fetoprotein and PIVKA-II, and negative hepatitis B and C serologies make this less likely

rejected.label: colorectal liver metastasis with portal vein tumor thrombus
rejected.why: while possible, the champion diagnosis is more general and encompasses this possibility

rejected.label: cystadenocarcinoma
rejected.why: the presence of a solid component in the liver tumor and the patient's history of colon cancer make this less likely

rejected.label: intrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma
rejected.why: no communication with the biliary tree and negative bile cytology make this less likely
